title: Vibing a Peng clone starring Scorpion
author: blackwidowink
selftext:
Hi guys,

I decided to create a Peng clone where you play as Scorpion from Mortal Kombat. Why? I don’t know, it just seemed like a good idea at the time. I’m about 50% done, lots of levels and features to add. What do you think, should I keep going?

Code and some assets generated on Astrocade.com. Game backgrounds generated in Gemini using Nano Banana. The animations for Scorpion were made on Autosprite.io. Music was generated on Producer.ai. 

If you feel so inclined you can try it out [here](https://www.astrocade.com/games/bubble-kombat/01KCZ075GQ8S98BCRA538KKQCK?sharedByCreator=blackwidowink)

Let me know if you have any questions about to process, tips or ideas. I’m always open!

comments.author: DisasterNarrow4949
comments.body: I actually love this. Well done.

comments.author: sharkymcstevenson2
comments.body: This looks awesome, what’s your workflow?

replies.author: blackwidowink
replies.body:
Thanks! Generally I plan my games out using Claude to bounce some ideas off of. Then once I’m all dialed in I will generate a couple different initial prototypes on Astrocade to see how close we can get right off the bat. 

It might seem backwards, but I do like seeing the animations for the player character early on and then build around that. I either generate my animations with Astrocade’s own animation API or head over to Autosprite.

From there I lock down the main game play mechanics first until I’m satisfied and then it’s a lot of bouncing between the platforms I mentioned to get what I want and polishing the little things. I rarely look at the code these days, unless there’s something I really can’t get to work.
